# Review — ani-015-a

## Pass 1

Units are numbered from 0 in the order of `sentences`; word numbers are positions in the draft's word list (0-based).
Sign codes and order untouched; after editing: JSON loads, the sign sequence equals the packet's (919 glyphs), morph `g` covers every glyph of every word exactly once.

### Changes
- U20 (sk·n·s pḥ sw stꜣ·tw) · n, l, i · major · pḥ sw was read 'he arrives' "with sw as subject as in later Egyptian": the dependent pronoun after a verb is its object (later Egyptian puts sw first, not after the verb), so the label was wrong and the translation followed Budge against the grammar · note now reads pḥ sw '(it) reaches him', bark still the unwritten subject, notes the old passive 'he is reached' as possible and says why Budge's 'he arriveth' is not followed; l "reaches · him", i "…has hauled on(?) and reaches him; he is towed along."
- U0 · n · minor · r ḫpr ḥtp·f labelled "r 'until' with the infinitive"; r + infinitive is 'to', 'until' belongs to r + sḏmt·f · now "r 'to' with the infinitive… 'to the coming about of his setting', that is, until he sets"; l/i kept.
- U9 · n · minor · subjectless ḥtp called "the infinitive used of what goes on at the time", not a real category · now the stative with ending unwritten, '(you) being set', as the draft itself takes ḥtp in U30.
- U10 · i · minor · i dropped the m of m nb·i ('as my lord') that l keeps · i "…O lord, living and enduring as my lord."
- U12 · n · minor · nswt with t and n after the sedge called "an honorific spelling"; it is the normal spelling · "the usual spelling of the word".
- U14 · glyphs (w95 mꜣꜥt), n · minor · plinth Aa11 marked as a classifier and the sickle/U15 as plain phonograms; the house (mꜣꜥ-ḫrw, Plate 1) has U1 and ꜥ as complements of the phonogram Aa11 mꜣꜥ · U1 comp mꜣ, U15 comp ꜥ, X1 phon t, Aa11 phon mꜣꜥ; note rewritten to match.
- U16 · n, l, i · minor · "ḫpr is a sḏm·f with mr dsds as its subject": a noun subject before the verb with no resumptive suffix is subject + stative · stative, ending unwritten; l "has-come-into-being", i "the Lake of Desdes has come to be at peace."
- U16 · say (w103 dsds) · style · "Desdes" broke the say rule (e between consonants, as Seketet) and no published form exists · "Desedes"; English name Desdes kept in l/i.
- U18 · n · style · "with q, a knife and U15 as classifiers" made q a classifier · "with q, and then a knife and U15 as classifiers".
- U19 · n · minor · t of mꜣꜥw left unread without saying Budge reads it (maāt) · added "(Budge reads maāt, with the t)".
- U22 · glyphs (w130 pꜣwty) · minor · G41 marked comp of a log X6 'pꜣwt'; a biliteral is not a complement, and the published pꜣwt (Spell 17) has the bird as phon pꜣ with X6 X6 as classifiers · G41 phon pꜣ, X6 det, X6 det; note says both disks are classifiers.
- U22 · l · style · l "who-sends-forth" vs i "who sent forth" · l "who-sent-forth".
- U25 · glyphs (w153 psḏt) · style · X6 log psḏt + X1 comp t, where every published part has X6 log psḏ + X1 phon t · aligned.
- U27 · n · style · t of š left unread without a reason · "š is a masculine noun and the t is not read (Budge: śet)".
- U31 · morph (w189), n · minor · reading stwt·k under lemma sti 'shoot' (stwt·k is no form of sti) · lemma stwt with an occurrence gloss "to shine, send out rays (verb made from stwt 'rays' and spelled like it)"; note matched.
- U34 · reading, say, morph gloss, n, l, i (w215) · minor · the printed chick w was set aside to force the infinitive dwꜣ, against the signs and Budge (ṭuau); the infinitive of dwꜣ has no ending · read dwꜣw 'adoration' (lemma dwꜣ, occurrence gloss; the known dwꜣw is 'tomorrow', a different word), say duau; l "adoration · of-Osiris…", i "Adoration of Osiris, lord of everlastingness:".
- U36 · l, i, n · minor · "Iunu" for iwnw; the model and nearly every published part render it Heliopolis · Heliopolis in l/i, note "iwnw 'Heliopolis' (Iunu)".
- U37 · i · minor · l has the active sḏm·f "joins(?) he", i turned it passive "he is joined(?) with" · i "he joins(?) Memphis."

### Findings refused (draft kept)
- w64 itrty (drafter's doubt): N5 N5 cannot spell itrty, but no reading comes from the two discs alone either; Budge's àterti with his (?) is the only check, the note says plainly that no sound sign is written and gives the alternative; l/i carry (?). Kept.
- w146 pḥrrw: walking man as a word-sign is a guess, but it is stated as Budge's (?) reading with the same doubt, l/i carry (?). Kept.
- w45 nmi with bracket-only [k]: no sign to correct; misprint rule needs a sign to stand against, and the note already says the suffix is unwritten and '(you)' is supplied from line 8. Kept as is.
- w260 ḏꜥm vs Budge's smu: kept ḏꜥm (house practice: an approximate code takes the value of the sign it is taken to be, as in Plate 2), now with (?) and the M21/smw alternative stated (see changes).
- w238 ḫw·sn: reading kept (signs give ḫ-w, not Budge's ꜣḫ 'glorify'); only roles changed.
- U38 nṯrw pw sšm dwꜣt: 'A pw B' with the gods as subject is grammatical and makes ·sn in the next unit refer back; Budge's 'he hath created … the gods' is noted. Kept with "are(?)".
- U37 ḫnm·f: sense doubtful, both senses given; kept (only i voice fixed).
- U20 sk·n·s: sense 'haul' taken from Budge with (?), as in the published Plate 2 sk·n·f. Kept.
- U18 misprints qꜣs (w110) and ḥsq (w111): the Plate 1 parallel ꜥwy·f qꜣs and the published ḥsq spellings leave one reading each; notes open "The papyrus writes X; read Y." Kept.
- Printed signs not reflected in readings — reeds in ḥtpw (w48), vulture in ḫftyw·k (w50), mḥtyw (w125), imntyw (w126), second t in iꜣbtyw (w127), t in mꜣꜥw (w117), reed in trwy (w97), w in stꜣ·tw (w123), w in sḥr·s (w248), strokes in skr (w226) and ḥpt (w243), U15 in sḫr: each keeps its sound value (phon with tr) or is a classifier, and the note says the reading does not use it, which is the published practice (ḫftyw·f with G1 phon ꜣ in Spells 1, 17, 18; trwy; qꜣs w). Kept.
- U3 "(my)" in l/i for the unwritten suffix: clearly marked as supplied. Kept.
